messages:
From: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>

Subject: Strategy Ops: Competitive intel digest & QBR prep — action items

Team,

Quick roundup ahead of next week's QBR/OKR check-ins — pulled together from market signals and a couple external notes (see attachments). High-level takeaways and asks below. Please read end-to-end; I want a short deck for the Exec QBR by Tues morning.

Key market moves (last 72h):
- Pricing: BenchAI announced a 20% list-price reduction on their hosted text-inference SKU and a new committed-reserved price tier (see competitor-pricing-matrix.pdf). Likely targeted at mid-market PLG accounts.
- Model releases: LlamaX 70B (quantized inference flow) posted an official release this AM — claims sub-100ms 1k-token throughput on NVIDIA A100 via new kernels (attached model-release-brief.docx; source press release included).
- Positioning: Rival suppliers are leaning hard into "cost-first" messaging (lower TCO, prebuilt caching). Their marketing emphasizes easy migration from larger models.

Immediate asks (owners):
- Product (Karthik): rapid impact assessment — latency/cost delta if customers switch to LlamaX-70/quantized variants; compatibility notes for our runtime and fallback story. Deliverable: 1-pager + impact matrix by EOD Mon.
- Sales (Laura): short messaging and pricing playbook (2 slides) to counter BenchAI move for AMER mid-market portfolio. Include recommended concessions we can make without breaking OKRs.
- Engineering/Infra (Markus): quick note on any infra risk (capacity or new kernel work) and whether Dedicated customers are exposed.

Logistics:
- Prep call: Mon 11/02 10:00 AM PT (30m) — sync on slide deck and decision points.
- Add to QBR exec packet: top 3 competitive threats + ask for one directional exec decision (pricing credit vs targeted incentives).

Attachments: [Attachment: competitor-pricing-matrix.pdf (PDF, 92KB)], [Attachment: model-release-brief.docx (DOCX, 48KB)]

Thanks — keep responses short and action-focused.

Cheers,
Stephanie Nguyen
VP, Strategy & GTM Operations
Redwood Inference

Subject: Re: Strategy Ops: Competitive intel digest & QBR prep — action items

Thanks Stephanie — skimmed the attachments. Quick notes:

- BenchAI price tiering looks like an aggressive volume play. If true adoption is limited to small LTV accounts, impact is low; if they push reserved tiers into larger deals, we need sales guidance.
- LlamaX 70B: the press-release claims are unsurprising; our runtime already supports similar quantization paths but the new kernel variants may affect our perf estimates.

Karthik — can you call out which of our models/mode-configs are most at risk (e.g., 13B vs 70B)? Prioritize customers on Reserved/Dedicated that have recent RPS growth.

Forwarding an external analyst note I received that flags the same themes — FYI.

To: Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>

FYI — BenchAI is rolling aggressive list reductions. They want to own the "drop-in, low-cost inference" narrative for mid-market SaaS. For larger customers they'll push reserved discounts. Expect a push in AMER next 30 days.

-Sam

From: Karthik Iyer <karthik_iyer@redwood.ai>
To: Stephanie Nguyen <stephanie_nguyen@redwood.ai>, Markus Klein <markus_klein@redwood.ai>, Laura Bennett <laura_bennett@redwood.ai>
Date: Mon, 02 Nov 2026 08:07:00 -0700
Subject: Re: Strategy Ops: Competitive intel digest & QBR prep — action items

Stephanie/Markus/Laura — initial assessment below (will attach a short matrix).

Summary: LlamaX-70B release primarily threatens mid-market and self-serve flows where teams optimize for cost per token. The kernel improvements reduce some of the hedging we recommend (smaller models + caching). For our enterprise customers (Reserved/Dedicated), risk is lower but not zero — customers already benchmarking several models.

Impact matrix (high level):
- 13B configs (our default mid-tier): medium risk — cheaper 70B variants may flip some late-stage deals where latency/cost are decisive.
- 70B-equivalent configs: low immediate risk; their claim is about quantized inference which benefits very specific workloads.
- Dedicated/Private: low risk but we need to validate supported kernels; some customers will demand parity.

Action items from Product (deliverable: model-impact-matrix.xlsx):
- Provide benchmark delta (latency/cost) for 13B/70B quantized vs our 13B quantized + LRU caching by EOD Mon.
- Call out any missing kernel/runtime changes that would prevent feature parity.
- Short list of mitigation options: 1) targeted price hold for top-20 mid-market accounts; 2) tighter caching defaults; 3) bundle support/observability as a differentiator.

I will drop the attached impact matrix in the sync.

-Karthik
Director, Product Management
Redwood Inference
